candidates.summary: RegisterExtension freezes the hook's kind so an entry cannot re-key itself, but checks view.ExtensionKind() and view.TokenID() only once; the published view keeps answering live, so GetExtension(key, k) can hand out a view that now reports another kind or another token
candidates.failure_scenario: Issuer registers a view whose ExtensionKind and TokenID read through pointers (the shiftyExtension shape token_test uses for the hook), then changes them. tok.ExtensionView("aux") and grc721reg.GetExtension(key, "aux") return a view whose ExtensionKind() is "mock" and whose TokenID() is another collection's ID; a consumer that trusts the registration check ("view belongs to another token") reads the wrong collection. The diff swept this class for the hook (registeredExtension.kind) and left the view's two self-reports unfrozen.
candidates.verify_by: Add to token_test.gno: a shiftyView{kind *string, tid *string}; RegisterExtension(shiftyExtension{&k}, shiftyView{&k2,&tid}) with k2==k and tid==tok.ID(); then set k2="mock", tid="other"; assert tok.ExtensionView("aux").ExtensionKind()=="aux" and TokenID()==tok.ID(); observe both fail.

candidates.summary: Register's slug is validated and emitted in the register event, and nothing else: it is not the key, not stored, not returned by Get or GetRegistry, and not rendered, so a consumer of the registry can never resolve or display it
candidates.failure_scenario: A realm registers with slug "cool-apes"; Get("cool-apes"), Render and GetRegistry know nothing of it, and only an indexer replaying events sees it. The parameter costs callers a validation panic (slug too long, invalid character) for a value with no on-chain reader.
candidates.verify_by: grep -n slug examples/gno.land/r/demo/defi/grc721reg/grc721reg.gno: hits only at 33 (signature), 38-39 (validate), 72 (event attr), 291-298 (validateSlug).
candidates.evidence: grep -n 'slug' grc721reg.gno returned lines 33, 38, 39, 57 (comment), 72, 291, 292, 293, 296, 298; no registry.Set, Get or render use

candidates.summary: Every grc721reg test runs inside one test function under testing.SetRealm; no txtar or filetest has an issuer realm package register its token in init and then mint or attach an extension in a later transaction while a separate consumer realm reads GetExtension, the shape grc20reg pins in grc20_registry_wrappers.txtar
candidates.failure_scenario: The token and its ledger are handed to grc721reg's registry.Set in the issuer's init; whether the issuer can still Mint and RegisterExtension on objects grc721reg now references, and whether a consumer realm can call a view method across the boundary in a later tx, is asserted nowhere. TestRegisteredCollectionStaysLive claims late attach reaches consumers but never crosses a transaction or a persisted realm boundary.
candidates.verify_by: Write gno.land/pkg/integration/testdata/grc721_registry.txtar modeled on grc20_registry_wrappers.txtar: addpkg an issuer realm whose init does NewToken, NewRoyalty and grc721reg.Register; gnokey maketx call a Mint wrapper in a later tx; addpkg a consumer realm calling grc721reg.GetExtension(key, "royalty").(*royalty.Royalty).RoyaltyInfo; run go test ./gno.land/pkg/integration -run TestTestdata/grc721_registry and expect every step OK.
candidates.evidence: grep -rln grc721reg over examples and gno.land/pkg/integration/testdata: only grc721reg's own files and a tellers.gno comment; grc20reg has foo20, wugnot and grc20_registry_wrappers.txtar
